content.text:
I couldn't open any files, so this diagnosis comes from the standard NestJS boilerplate layout and the file names. The line numbers are estimates and the code itself is unchecked.

The likely cause is that a partial update with no `photo` in the payload gets treated as "clear the photo". This would happen in the update path for `PATCH /auth/me`. That path goes through `AuthService.update`, then `UsersService.update`, then the repository `update`, which uses the mapper's `toPersistence`.

candidates.explanation: The photo handling in update most likely treats an absent photo (undefined) the same as an explicit null. When only firstName is sent, photo ends up null or undefined and is written back, so the avatar link is cleared. Only an explicit `photo: null` should clear it. An absent photo should be left out of the payload.

If the photo branch falls through to setting `photo = null` whenever domainEntity.photo is falsy, instead of only when it is explicitly null, every partial update nulls the photo relation. The merged entity `{...existing, ...payload}` can lose `photo`, and the mapper then persists that as null. An undefined photo should stay undefined so the relation is untouched.

The update merges the payload into the domain entity and saves the whole mapped entity. If the merge or mapping drops or overwrites `photo` when it is absent from the payload, the avatar is lost on any partial profile edit.

fix.description: In UsersService.update, only touch photo when the payload contains it. Resolve the file when `photo?.id` is present. Set null only when `photo === null` is explicit. Otherwise leave photo undefined. In UserMapper.toPersistence, set the photo entity to null only for an explicit null, and leave it undefined when absent so TypeORM or Mongoose does not overwrite the relation.
